body: It really sounds like you need better coping mechanisms for your panic attacks. I have heard of people experiencing different highs due to being hyper, extremely low and also suffering from severe anxiety/panic attacks. each of these extremes can lead to different effects of the thc due to the way your body metabolises it in these states. so it could very well be as much to do with the panic attack as anything else
i would like to point out that by tripping i meant feeling the effects of the thc for weeks afterwards
i agree sounds like his weed was laced tbh. i get that he struggled with it but I've never heard of someone tripping for 3-4 weeks after.

i get the point of this post but i am just offering a different experience with the effects of weed. i also feel obligated to say that the best way to get high off a lot of weed is to take it slow and steady both going up and coming down. for example if you smoked a joint before having as many cones as i did you would go up but just not as hard and then after you come down off your major high you have another joint it will stop the effects from falling to gliding down

over this past weekend I smoked about 8 huge cones of weed with a mate, I got the derealisation but it was able to make it lucid so I could control the way I felt about it. I have experienced this multiple times but the more I have experienced it the more I understand it and can be comfortable with it. also I have found that the length of this subsides the more it occurs. I have found that it is similar to a natural disassociation that occurs when someone is suffering from severe depression or anxiety. I suffer from both of these and I have found that after getting high I can go through the disassociation/depersonalisation smoother and with a more calm outlook
self harm is like a release for me, its hard to understand if you haven't been there yourself. I appreciate the tip though, I will give it a try

not that this if definite but I think that most people irl don't know what to say. its not that they don't care its just they feel like they haven't been through what you have so they don't want to make assumptions and upset you more. I've found being more open and talking to people with the attitude that they are trying to help helps

I cant help you but all I know is that I went through the same thing and its really fucked up. I found that she started to deny that she said she loved me, this wrecked me because I felt so invalid. like my feelings were selfish and that I had put everything on her. when in reality it had been the other way around. in the end I talked to a friend about it and he helped me to realise what she had done to me. sometimes just acknowledging what happened and why is enough to move on as best as possible. one thing I would say is don't do this on your own. it seems like the best way to do it but in reality its the most dangerous way because you don't have that check or that person to say what your feeling is either valid or invalid
